subject: literature

source.track: IGCSE · ages 14–16 · all candidates take Paper 1 Poetry and Prose and either Paper 2 Drama or Component 3 Coursework

note: The syllabus teaches by form and skill, so units run close reading first, then the three main forms the assessment names (poetry, prose, drama) in Paper order. Set texts rotate each year, so units anchor the skills and anthologies; a closing atlas-only unit tracks live lessons beyond the 0475 set-text course.

program.title: Close reading: how language creates meaning and effect
topics: Close reading of set texts, unseen texts and literary extracts
How language is used to create meanings and effects
Diction, imagery and the sentence-level case
Figures of speech and their purpose
Writing a well-structured essay
Using quotations and references to support ideas

program.title: Poetry (Paper 1, Section A)
topics: Section A: Poetry — candidates study all 15 poems from the chosen text
Songs of Ourselves, Volume 1: from Shakespeare's Sonnet 18 to Heaney's Follower
Songs of Ourselves, Volume 3: from Clare's Insects to Amadiume's Mistress of My Own Being
Kayo Chingonyi: Kumukanda
Form, language and structure in poetry

program.title: Prose (Paper 1, Section B)
topics: Section B: Prose — candidates study the whole text
Set novels: from Austen's Pride and Prejudice to Lloyd Banwo's When We Were Birds
Stories of Ourselves, Volume 3: from Hardy's Tony Kytes to Abdullah's Reflection
Plot, narrative shape and tension
The novel as a developing form

program.title: Drama (Paper 2)
topics: Section A: Drama — candidates study one whole set text
J B Priestley: An Inspector Calls
William Shakespeare: The Tempest
Oscar Wilde: The Importance of Being Earnest
Pearl Cleage: Blues for an Alabama Sky
Chinonyerem Odimba: Princess & The Hustler

program.title: Wider literary study: atlas extension
topics: World epics: Gilgamesh, Iliad, Mahabharata, Sundiata
Literary theory: formalism to postcolonialism
Modernism and postmodernism
Comparative literature and translation
Textual criticism and scholarly editions
